newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end sharply up, near new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end sharply up, near new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures surged to sharply higher closes after posting new contract highs in February and April on short-covering demand prompted by stronger cash markets and fund buying, traders said.

Live cattle closed 1.200 to 0.325 cent per lb higher with April up most at 67.775 cents after posting a new high of 67.975 cents. February settled 1.075 cent higher at 66.750 cents after setting a new high of 66.975 cents earlier.

Packers paid $65 per cwt for fed cattle in Plains area direct trade, up $1, which sparked a short-covering rally. The rally triggered buy stops and prompted fund buying that took futures sharply higher, traders said.
Packer interest for cattle was up following a firmer tone to boxed beef with feedlots current in their marketings and reduced cattle weights adding to cash strength.

"They're (cattle weights) down compared to where they were a year ago and a week ago so maybe the packer needs a few more for the tonnage situation," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst for Securities Corporation of Iowa.
USDA estimated the average weight of slaughter cattle last week at 1,163 lbs, down slightly from 1,164 the previous week and well below the actual weight of 1,177 lbs a year earlier.

Maher also speculated that packer demand for cattle could be up because beef exports may have risen. Domestic demand for beef is not strong enough during Lent to account for the aggressive packer buying interest, he said.

Traders also cited action in futures Tuesday after USDA's cattle report on Friday. April futures were stronger than expected and back months not down as much as expected. This offset much of the report's bearishness, they said.

Futures pushed through technical resistance and prompted fund and stop loss buying that boosted nearbys to new contract highs. Feeder cattle followed on spillover support that offset another day of gains in corn futures. Short covering in feeder cattle also lifted prices into buy stops, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index climbed $0.03 to $68.90 per cwt.

Cargill Investor Services, Dean Witter and R.J. O'Brien notably bought April live cattle late while Rosenthal Collins and RBH sold. In live cattle options, commission houses bought April 64 puts and 68 and 70 calls, pit sources said.
Cargill also bought March feeders late while Refco sold May feeders, traders said. E.D.&F. Man and LIT division of First Options were featured buyers early, sources said.
E.D.&F. Man also was a buyer of fall contracts while selling spring contracts, pit sources added.
